claim: RAM data is always encrypted when it is moved to the EBS root volume; root volume encryption is enforced at instance launch.

claim: To use hibernation, the root volume must be an encrypted EBS volume with enough free space to hold the memory contents, and the instance must be configured for hibernation.
question: What are the prerequisites to hibernate an instance?

values.display: the root volume must be an encrypted EBS volume
values.spoken: root must be an encrypted EBS volume

values.display: sufficient space available on your EBS root volume
values.spoken: enough room on the root volume for RAM

evidence.quote: To use hibernation, the root volume must be an encrypted EBS volume. The instance needs to be configured to receive the ACPID signal for hibernation (or use the Amazon published AMIs that are configured for hibernation). Additionally, your instance should have sufficient space available on your EBS root volume to write data from memory.

claim: Hibernation cannot be enabled on an existing instance, running or stopped; it must be enabled at instance launch.

enabled during instance launch

evidence.quote: No, you cannot enable hibernation on an existing instance (running or stopped). This needs to be enabled during instance launch.

claim: If the EBS root volume does not have enough space for the memory contents, hibernation fails and the instance is shut down instead.
question: What happens if the EBS root volume is too small to hold RAM during hibernation?

values.display: hibernation will fail
the instance will get shut down instead

evidence.quote: If the EBS root volume does not have enough space, hibernation will fail and the instance will get shut down instead.

claim: Hibernation suits applications that take a long time to bootstrap: pre-warmed instances can be resumed to reduce the time to return to service, because hibernation retains memory state across stop and start.
question: Why would you hibernate an instance instead of stopping it?

values.display: take a long time to bootstrap
Hibernation retains memory state across Stop/Start cycles

evidence.quote: You can hibernate an instance to get your instance and applications up and running quickly, if they take a long time to bootstrap (e.g. load memory caches). You can start instances, bring them to a desired state and hibernate them. These “pre-warmed” instances can then be resumed to reduce the time it takes for an instance to return to service. Hibernation retains memory state across Stop/Start cycles.

claim: For High Memory instances, virtualized instances are generally recommended; metal instances are needed for unsupported OS versions, non-virtualized licensing or support needs, access to hardware features such as Intel VT-x, or a custom hypervisor such as ESXi.

evidence.quote: Though High Memory ‘Virtualized’ instances are in-general recommended to be used, there are specific situations where only High Memory Metal instances can work. These situations include – when using OS versions that are not supported on High Memory Virtual instances OR when using applications that need to run in non-virtualized mode to meet licensing / support requirements OR when using applications that require access to hardware feature set (such as Intel VT-x) OR when using custom hypervisor (e.g, ESXi).

VPC networking and EBS storage resources are implemented by dedicated hardware components, Nitro Cards that are part of all current generation EC2 instance families.

claim: Instances on the Nitro Hypervisor support at most 27 additional PCI devices shared by EBS volumes and VPC network interfaces; for example, 3 additional network interfaces leave room for 24 EBS volumes.

up to 24 EBS volumes

qualifiers.scope: instances on the Nitro Hypervisor, additional EBS volumes plus network interfaces
qualifiers.condition: the user guide states a shared attachment limit for most Nitro types; see the volume limits facts

evidence.quote: Instances running on the Nitro Hypervisor support a maximum of 27 additional PCI devices for EBS volumes and VPC ENIs. Each EBS volume or VPC ENI uses a PCI device. For example, if you attach 3 additional network interfaces to an instance that uses the Nitro Hypervisor, you can attach up to 24 EBS volumes to that instance.
